title: Contested requests: objections, a factfinder and report-backs
question: When a union or the Commission pushed back on contracting out, what did the record show?
finding: 6 requests went to the Commission’s regular agenda as separate items, worth $86.4 million. In one, a factfinder found the transportation agency had not shown a compelling reason, and the agency acknowledged it did no formal study of using City staff; in two, the Commission had asked the department to look at doing the work itself, and both departments recommended staying with the contractor.
how: The separate staff reports in the packets, read in full. Quotations are at most 25 words of the department’s or the factfinder’s text as stored.
limits: These are the contested cases, not a sample: most requests pass on the ratification agenda without debate. A factfinder’s recommendation is advisory; the Commission decides. Union statements are the union’s position.

rows.what: Approved in May 2024 on condition that the utility study bringing the work in-house and report back; the utility recommends continuing with the contractor.
rows.quote: “There is no existing classification and staffing budget available to hire new or existing exempt staff for purposes of the…”

rows.work: Operation and maintenance of the Terminal 2 baggage system and passenger boarding bridges
rows.what: Third annual report after Stationary Engineers Local 39 appealed, saying its classes can do the work; the Airport recommends the work stay with the contractor.
rows.quote: “Therefore, the Airport respectfully recommends that its baggage handling system maintenance job functions continue to be managed by contract.”

rows.what: A factfinder found on 24 December 2025 that the request lacked the specificity to show a compelling reason to contract out; the agency split the work into two categories and resubmitted. Of $15 million on the earlier engineering contracts, just under $9 million had been spent.
rows.quote: “SFMTA acknowledges that it did not undertake a formal study to determine whether it would be feasible to have City employees perform…”

rows.work: Professional services for the City’s permit platform (OpenGov), 72 months
rows.what: IFPTE Local 21 objected; the union did not ask for factfinding in time and the request went forward. The form adds $21,994,772 of software licences beside the services.
rows.quote: “This request formalizes and expands the professional services framework for OpenGov, the City's permit platform.”

rows.work: Construction and programme management for capital projects, 48 months
rows.what: IFPTE Local 21 objected on 15 June 2026; the utility met the union, which did not ask for a factfinder, and the request went forward.
rows.quote: “the SFPUC will seek to in-house this work as well, but there are not currently resources to do it within the agency.”

rows.work: Supplemental registered nurses from staffing registries, 12 months
rows.what: SEIU Local 1021 objected, pointing to the Per Diem nurse class and to registry spending the department could not split by class; the department told the union all City positions had been frozen since 20 March 2026.
rows.quote: “this PSC is for intermittent nursing work for which the City already has a specific classification, the Per Diem 2320.”

sources.t: San Francisco Civil Service Commission: agenda attachments over 8 MB, November 2022 to November 2026 (personal-services contract requests and staff reports)
